frameworks.name: Flask (clean-slate: Flask 3.1.3 + flask-smorest 0.47.0 + marshmallow 4.4.0 + Waitress 3.0.2 / Werkzeug)
advantages: Zero native toolchain blockers on Chaquopy 17.2 + Python 3.13: Flask, Werkzeug, Jinja2, Click, ItsDangerous, Blinker, Waitress, flask-smorest, Marshmallow, webargs, and apispec are all 100% pure-Python wheels; the sole native dep MarkupSafe 3.0.4 publishes official cp313 android_24_arm64_v8a and x86_64 wheels on PyPI and chaquo.com/pypi-13.1/.
Synchronous WSGI shares SQLite connections cleanly with existing background scheduler threads (threading.Thread / APScheduler) without asyncio event-loop contention or main-thread OS signal crashes.

flask-smorest 0.47.0 provides FastAPI-like declarative schemas, automatic OpenAPI 3.0 JSON generation (usable for Flutter Dart client codegen), Swagger UI, and structured validation purely via Marshmallow — without Pydantic/Rust.
Ultra-light wheel weight (~603 KB core Flask stack + ~148 KB flask-smorest/marshmallow/webargs/apispec + 54.9 KB Waitress); fast minimal module import path.
disadvantages: Schema definitions use Marshmallow Field classes rather than native Python dataclass/Pydantic type hints, slightly more verbose than FastAPI.
WARNING on plugin choice: APIFlask 3.1.3 CANNOT be used cleanly on Chaquopy because it hard-depends on pydantic[email]>=2.0 (pulls blocked pydantic-core).

No built-in async concurrency benefits if a future screen ever streamed many external sockets concurrently (mitigated for 12 download channels via polite 1 req/s background worker threads or httpx sync Client).
app.run(debug=True, use_reloader=True) crashes on Chaquopy (chaquopy#1235); must run werkzeug.serving.make_server(..., threaded=True) or Waitress in a daemon thread.

ecosystem.validation_and_openapi: flask-smorest 0.47.0 + marshmallow 4.4.0 + webargs 8.7.1 + apispec 6.10.1 (all pure Python, https://flask-smorest.readthedocs.io/en/latest/). Avoid apiflask 3.1.3 (pulls pydantic>=2.0, https://apiflask.com/). Pure-Python dataclass option: dacite 1.9.3 (16.6 KB) or attrs 26.1.0 + cattrs 26.2.1.
ecosystem.auth: flask-httpauth 4.8.1 (9.4 KB pure Python) or trivial shared-secret localhost header middleware (single-user offline app has no user accounts).
ecosystem.scheduler: APScheduler 3.11.3 BackgroundScheduler (64.5 KB pure Python, https://pypi.org/project/APScheduler/) or stdlib threading.Thread daemon loop — native match for sync WSGI.
ecosystem.serving: Waitress 3.0.2 (54.9 KB pure-Python production WSGI, https://docs.pylonsproject.org/projects/waitress/en/stable/) or werkzeug.serving.make_server(threaded=True).

frameworks.name: FastAPI 0.165.0 (+ Starlette 1.10.0 + Pydantic 2.14.4 + pydantic-core 2.50.5 + Uvicorn 0.54.0)
advantages: Best-in-class API DX on standard servers: native Python type hints drive Pydantic validation, serialization, dependency injection, and OpenAPI 3.1 schema generation for Flutter codegen.
Rich modern async ecosystem (async/await endpoints, BackgroundTasks, WebSockets, SSE).
Clean modular APIRouter architecture suited to greenfield API-first design.
disadvantages: HARD INSTALL BLOCKER ON CHAQUOPY 17.2 + PYTHON 3.13: FastAPI 0.165.0 requires pydantic>=2.9.0 -> pydantic-core==2.50.5 (Rust/PyO3). Live check 2026-11-26 confirms 0/139 PyPI wheels target Android and https://chaquo.com/pypi-13.1/pydantic-core/ returns HTTP 404. Chaquopy issue #1017 ('pydantic v2') is OPEN; PR #1413 closed unmerged with maintainer declining new Chaquopy native recipes in favor of upstream PyPI Android wheels.

UNOFFICIAL WORKAROUNDS FRAGILE: Community wheel repo Eutalix/android-pydantic-core (16 stars) latest v2.50.0 only ships cp314 assets, missing cp313. Pinning EOL pure-Python Pydantic 1.10.21 freezes FastAPI to legacy releases (<0.100/v1 compat) and risks Python 3.13 incompatibilities.

Uvicorn thread trap: running uvicorn inside a Chaquopy daemon thread crashes with ValueError: signal only works in main thread unless subclassing uvicorn.Server to noop install_signal_handlers() (and omitting uvicorn[standard] native extras uvloop/httptools/watchfiles).

APK + import overhead: pure-Python graph (~1.19 MB compressed incl. opentelemetry-api 58.9 KB) plus custom pydantic-core (~1.46-2.47 MB per ABI x 2 ABIs = ~3-5 MB compressed). Async/sync SQLite friction (sync endpoints bounce through AnyIO threadpool). Exact Android cold-start ms UNVERIFIED.

ecosystem.scheduler: APScheduler 3.x / AsyncIOScheduler or FastAPI lifespan context + httpx.AsyncClient.
ecosystem.serving: Uvicorn 0.54.0 pure-Python (h11 + click + anyio), requires custom Server subclass disabling signal handlers in Chaquopy worker threads.

frameworks.name: Starlette 1.10.0 raw (+ Uvicorn 0.54.0 pure-Python, paired with Marshmallow or attrs/cattrs)
advantages: 100% pure-Python ASGI core (~578 KB combined across starlette 78.7 KB, uvicorn 85.4 KB, anyio 131.4 KB, h11 36.6 KB, idna 68 KB, sniffio 10 KB, click 123.2 KB, typing-extensions 44.5 KB; 0 native wheels if uvicorn[standard] is skipped).
Installs cleanly on Chaquopy (verified pure-Python in chaquopy#857; requires Python >=3.11, fits repo's 3.13).

disadvantages: No built-in request validation, serialization models, or automatic OpenAPI generation — requires bolting on pure-Python Marshmallow/apispec or attrs+cattrs manually (losing FastAPI's flagship reason to exist).
Still inherits Uvicorn's secondary-thread install_signal_handlers() override requirement on Android and ASGI-over-sync-sqlite3 threadpool bridging.
Smaller beginner plugin ecosystem for validation/OpenAPI compared to Flask-Smorest or FastAPI.

ecosystem.serving: Uvicorn 0.54.0 (pure-Python core) with custom install_signal_handlers() override.

frameworks.name: Python stdlib (Mode A: ThreadingHTTPServer / wsgiref, OR Mode B: Direct Python MethodChannel + dataclasses + sqlite3)
advantages: ZERO third-party framework risk and ZERO extra APK bytes: runs cleanly on any Chaquopy Python 3.10–3.15 version forever.
Ideal core engine for Mode B (direct Android MethodChannel -> Chaquopy Python dispatch): skips localhost TCP port management, HTTP parsing, and cleartext localhost security config entirely.
Smallest cold-start import graph possible (~milliseconds beyond CPython startup; exact device ms UNVERIFIED).
disadvantages: In Mode A (localhost HTTP), writing routing, path params, query parsing, CORS/error envelopes, and OpenAPI schema generation by hand on top of BaseHTTPRequestHandler or wsgiref adds boilerplate.
No Swagger UI or automatic OpenAPI generation without adding apispec/custom script.
In Mode B (no HTTP server), Flutter's standard REST clients (dio/http) and desktop curl/OpenAPI tooling cannot talk directly to endpoints unless wrapped in a thin HTTP shim for dev.

ecosystem.validation_and_openapi: stdlib dataclasses + typing + json + src/validators; optional pure-Python dacite 1.9.3 (16.6 KB) or marshmallow 4.4.0.
ecosystem.auth: None needed for Mode B JNI calls; manual header check in Mode A.
ecosystem.serving: Mode A: http.server.ThreadingHTTPServer / wsgiref.simple_server; Mode B: direct com.chaquo.python.Python module calls.

frameworks.on_device_status: 100% NATIVE / GUARANTEED COMPATIBLE across all ABIs and future Python upgrades.
frameworks.async_sync_fit: Pure synchronous; exact fit for sqlite3, urllib.request, csv, zipfile, xml.etree.ElementTree.
frameworks.learning_curve: Low for core Python; manual plumbing for HTTP route dispatch in Mode A.
frameworks.download_tooling_pairing: Can run 100% stdlib (urllib.request + csv + xml.etree + zipfile) with 0 KB deps, or add pure-Python httpx/requests/beautifulsoup4/openpyxl/feedparser cleanly.
frameworks.verdict: BEST CHOICE IF CHOOSING MODE B (MethodChannel bridge, no HTTP server); in Mode A (localhost HTTP), Flask + flask-smorest saves boilerplate for <0.8 MB.

localhost_http.description: Python starts a bound loopback HTTP server on 127.0.0.1:<port> inside a Kotlin/Java daemon thread; Flutter calls REST JSON endpoints via dart:io HttpClient / http / dio.
pros: Clean OpenAPI JSON contract + standard REST client tooling in Flutter (dio/http, Swagger/openapi-generator).
Backend remains desktop-runnable and directly testable with pytest / curl / Postman outside Android.
Decouples Flutter Dart UI cleanly from Chaquopy Kotlin boilerplate.
cons: Requires managing localhost port binding, startup readiness probe, Android cleartext loopback exception (127.0.0.1 in network_security_config.xml), and daemon thread lifecycle (no reloader/signals).
Minor localhost TCP + JSON serialization latency per call (negligible on single-user mobile vs UI render, exact ms UNVERIFIED).

platform_channel_bridge.description: No HTTP server at all: Flutter calls Android Kotlin via MethodChannel, Kotlin invokes Chaquopy Python functions directly through com.chaquo.python.Python JNI bridge and returns JSON strings/maps.
pros: Zero HTTP server dependency, zero open loopback ports, zero port conflicts or readiness polling, zero network_security_config cleartext rules.
Lowest memory & APK weight (~0.8 MB smaller than Flask+OpenAPI stack) and lowest IPC latency (in-process JNI vs loopback TCP).
Eliminates Werkzeug/Uvicorn thread signal-handler edge cases altogether.
cons: Android-locked architecture: couples API dispatch to Kotlin MethodChannel + Chaquopy Java API (cannot point Flutter desktop/test runner at a localhost URL without adding an HTTP wrapper).
Must run Chaquopy calls off Android UI main thread (Kotlin Coroutines Dispatchers.IO) or risk ANRs.
Loses automatic HTTP Swagger UI / standard OpenAPI REST client generation unless generated separately from Python dataclass/Marshmallow schemas.
best_frameworks: Pure Python stdlib router + dataclasses + sqlite3 (NO web framework needed)
Optional pure-Python Marshmallow 4.4.0 / dacite 1.9.3 for strict payload validation + apispec for OpenAPI docs

community_verdicts.verdict: Practitioners embedding Python HTTP APIs inside Android/desktop wrappers (Chaquopy, PyWebView) overwhelmingly favor lightweight synchronous WSGI (Flask with use_reloader=False / Werkzeug run_simple / Waitress or Bottle wsgiref) over FastAPI+Uvicorn, citing smaller APK weight, faster cold import, zero event-loop/signal-handler thread crashes, and avoidance of pydantic-core cross-compilation.

For Flutter + Android-only Chaquopy apps, community consensus prefers direct JNI MethodChannel invocation for simple local RPC when cross-platform portability isn't needed, OR localhost 127.0.0.1 HTTP (Flask/REST) when teams want standard Flutter http/dio clients, OpenAPI contracts, and desktop/CI testability.

Notable public Android projects shipping embedded Python/Flask stacks via Chaquopy include Twisted-Hell-7/pyroid (offline Android Python IDE supporting Flask), shivam-app-developers/codevarsity-mobile-ide (Chaquopy offline Python execution supporting Flask/Django), and davidchilin/werewolves_game (self-hosted local Flask APK via Chaquopy).

On standard servers, FastAPI wins clean-slate JSON API adoption via type-hinted Pydantic V2 + OpenAPI; in pure-Python/Marshmallow contexts where Pydantic is unavailable or undesirable, flask-smorest (Flask + Marshmallow + apispec) is the established OpenAPI-generating alternative (note APIFlask itself pulls Pydantic v2).

primary.choice: Clean-slate Flask 3.1.3 + flask-smorest 0.47.0 (Marshmallow + apispec OpenAPI) + Waitress 3.0.2 (or Werkzeug make_server daemon thread) on localhost HTTP, paired with pure-Python download tooling (httpx sync Client or stdlib urllib, beautifulsoup4+html.parser, feedparser, openpyxl read_only=True)
primary.fast_api_vs_flask_summary: Even starting from zero with all 41 old routes deleted, FastAPI is NOT viable out-of-the-box on Chaquopy Python 3.13 because pydantic-core 2.50.5 has 0 Android wheels on PyPI and 404 on Chaquopy. Flask + flask-smorest achieves the exact clean-slate goal Flutter needs (typed validated JSON contracts + automatic OpenAPI 3.0 spec for Dart codegen + Swagger UI) at <0.85 MB pure-Python wheel cost (plus official cp313 Android wheels for MarkupSafe) with zero Rust/NDK build risk and natural sync SQLite/scheduler harmony.

runner_up.choice_a_no_server: Mode B (Chaquopy JNI MethodChannel + Kotlin Dispatchers.IO + stdlib dataclasses/sqlite3 + optional Marshmallow/apispec) if the team wants to eliminate localhost HTTP servers, open ports, and WSGI dependencies completely (~0.8 MB leaner, zero loopback socket setup).
runner_up.choice_b_http_asgi: Pure-Python Starlette 1.10.0 + Uvicorn 0.54.0 (signal-patched, excluding uvicorn[standard]) + Marshmallow/cattrs — installs today on Chaquopy Python 3.13 (~578 KB) if async SSE streaming is prioritized, though weaker API DX than flask-smorest.

flip_conditions: FLIP TO FASTAPI AS PRIMARY if (1) pydantic-core publishes official cp313/cp314 android_24_arm64_v8a and x86_64 wheels on PyPI (or Chaquopy restores a prebuilt wheel in pypi-13.1), eliminating custom Rust/NDK cross-compilation CI — OR if the project upgrades Chaquopy to target Python 3.14 ONLY after Eutalix/upstream provides official cp314 arm64_v8a + x86_64 wheels AND teams accept subclassing Uvicorn signal handlers.

FLIP TO PURE STDLIB + METHODCHANNEL BRIDGE if Flutter integration decides against localhost HTTP clients (dio/http) and targets strictly Android-only in-process JNI calls without needing desktop REST testing or live Swagger UI.
